class.name: NetwSessionConfig
class.description: Settings are applied once, before assigning [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer] or starting a connection through [member NetwSession.connection]. Otherwise they apply at the end of the frame. Later changes warn and are ignored. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_session(self) \ .app(&"bomber-v2") \ .role(NetwSession.ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER) [/codeblock] [b]Bandwidth[/b] [member bandwidth_kbps] sets a bandwidth budget per peer. Updates that wait longer or have higher [member NetwEntity.replication_priority] are sent first. RPCs, spawns, authority changes and [method NetwPropertyConfig.retained] properties can exceed the budget. Other property updates still receive at least a quarter of each tick's budget. Later ticks repay the excess, up to two ticks of budget at a time.

method.name: app
method.description: Sets [member app_id] to identify the game and build.

method.name: bandwidth
method.description: Sets [member bandwidth_kbps], the bandwidth budget per peer in kbit/s.

method.name: role
method.description: Sets [member desired_role], the role this peer takes when it hosts.

method.name: server
method.description: Sets [member server_info], the information shown in server browsers.

method.name: transfer
method.description: Sets [member transfer_mode], which determines what happens to this peer's world when the server moves.

method.name: transfer_deadline
method.description: Sets [member transfer_deadline_ticks], how many ticks the new server waits for each client to report its world.

members.member: The game and build. Peers with a different [member app_id] cannot connect. Leave it empty to accept any. WebRTC room codes are also created per [member app_id].

The budget each peer is sent, in kbit/s. [code]0[/code] allows each peer one datagram a tick of [member SceneMultiplayer.max_sync_packet_size], less 150 bytes of headroom. A negative value is refused. While a peer loses packets its budget halves, and each round trip without loss adds back an eighth of it, up to this value. [method NetwSession.set_peer_bandwidth] gives one peer its own budget.
The role this peer takes when it hosts, which becomes [member NetwMultiplayer.role].

What this server shows in server browsers. The player count and [member NetwServerInfo.app_id] are filled in automatically. Copied when applied. [codeblock] var info := NetwServerInfo.new() info.motd = "Friday night" info.max_players = 8 Netw.configure_session(self).server(info) [/codeblock] To change it for each request, use [method Netw.configure_server_info].
How many ticks a new server waits for each client to report its world after the server moves. A client still reporting when it runs out is disconnected, and [code]0[/code] waits without a limit.

What this peer does with its world when the server moves. Each peer follows its own value, and a new server runs [method Netw.configure_transfer] only when its value is [constant NetwSession.TRANSFER_REJOIN].
